channel.title: Lumeshot
channel.description: Updates for Lumeshot, a screenshot and screen-recording tool for macOS.

item.description:
A maintenance release: a dozen fixes from two rounds of code review of v0.1.22, covering upload reliability and privacy, settings safety, and the annotation editor. No new features and no configuration changes — existing uploaders, settings and captures are unaffected.
## Settings and SSH safety
- A `settings.json` that exists but cannot be read (a permissions problem, a transient disk error) is no longer treated as an empty configuration. A preference change would previously overwrite the unreadable file with defaults, erasing your saved uploaders, filename template and pinned host keys; and an SSH host-key check could trust a new key as if none had been pinned. Both now stop and leave the file untouched rather than acting on defaults. - Editing General/Capture/Recording/Shortcut preferences no longer overwrites an SSH host key that a connection pinned at the same moment. - When two first-time SFTP uploads to the same destination race and the second server presents a different host key than the one just pinned, the second connection now fails closed instead of silently trusting it.
## Upload logging and result handling
- A failed SFTP upload no longer writes the server's status message to `~/Library/Logs/Lumeshot.log` — it can echo a remote path or a token. The SSH status code and the error type are kept. - A failed screen-recording upload no longer writes the raw server response to the log either, matching the redaction the still-image path already had. - A custom uploader whose server returns something that is not a web link — a `file:` URL, an app scheme, or an HTML error page — is now treated as a failed upload instead of being copied to the clipboard. History and notifications only open `http(s)` links, so an older entry can't launch a local file or another app. - A custom uploader response that leaves the image id empty is treated as a failed upload rather than copying a broken link such as `https://host/i/.png`.
## Annotation editor
- Resizing an annotation by dragging a handle past its opposite edge and back no longer drags the anchored edge along with it, so a crop keeps its intended size. - Increasing a text annotation's font size no longer pushes the text out of its box and drops it from the exported image; the box grows to fit the larger text. - Moving a crop against an image edge and back no longer permanently shrinks it. - The editor keeps its Cancel/Copy/Save/Upload buttons on screen at the smallest window size: the text, blur and pixelate controls now live in the left tool rail rather than crowding the top bar.
## File handling
- Lumeshot no longer advertises itself as an opener for MP4 and GIF files, which only produced an import error. Opening a file still imports `.sxcu` uploader configs.

One change: the editor now opens sized to the capture.
## The editor window fits what you captured
Instead of opening at a fixed size, the editor now sizes its window to the capture itself. A capture opens showing the image at 1:1 — the window is the image's on-screen size (its pixels divided by the display's scale factor) plus the tool rail and top bar. A capture larger than your display is capped to fit the screen (the canvas scales it down to show all of it), and a very small capture still opens at a comfortable minimum rather than a tiny window.
This replaces the remembered-size behaviour from v0.1.20/v0.1.21: the size now follows each capture rather than reusing the last one. The window remains freely resizable once open.

One change, to how the annotation editor's window is sized.
## The editor opens larger and remembers your size
The editor window opened small enough that marking up a capture felt cramped, and if you resized it the size was forgotten by the next capture.
It now opens at a generous default — up to 1200×780, capped to fit your screen and never smaller than 760×480 — and it **remembers the size and position you set**, so a one-time resize sticks for the next capture and the next launch. The window has always been resizable; this just gives it a roomier starting size and makes your own size stick.
